title: Oct 15, 2026AnnouncementsAn update on independent evaluators
summary: Announcements An update on independent evaluators Oct 15, 2026 Last month, we committed to stronger independent, third-party assessment of our models and safety practices. We also signed the White House Accord on Super Intelligence, in which companies pledged to partner with independent external auditors or evaluators. Today, we’re announcing that we’ve started to give employee-like access to a team from METR , a nonprofit that evaluates frontier AI models. METR will publish the results of its risk assessments. Over the past year, we’ve worked with METR on several reviews of our Risk Reports . We’re also working with SecureBio and Accenture as evaluators, and are in early discussions with several other organizations, including Hugging Face . Here, we explain our approach to working with evaluators. Why we work with independent evaluators As models have become more powerful, they’ve required stronger safeguards and more challenging risk assessments. We want to be publicly accountable for the decisions we’re making. But we can’t publicly share all the information relevant to our safety work. Some of it could be useful to malicious actors, or is commercially sensitive, like compute or training information. Instead, we’re giving third-party evaluators deep access to our information, and are having them share evidence and reasoned conclusions about the risks involved in building our models. We aim to close the gap between what evaluators understand about a frontier AI company’s systems and what the company itself understands. To evaluate frontier models, evaluators need the following: Expertise in assessing the capabilities of frontier models, including understanding the way evaluations can go wrong, such as alignment faking . Independence : they shouldn’t hold equity in the company they’re evaluating, or be financially or operationally dependent on it. Enough access to meaningfully evaluate risks. Beyond access to the latest models, evaluators also need visibility into
title_es: Anthropic se abre a evaluadores independientes externos
bajada: Anthropic comienza a dar acceso de investigador a equipos de METR para evaluar independientemente sus modelos y prácticas de seguridad, en línea con el White House Accord. También colabora con SecureBio y Accenture en evaluaciones de riesgo.
bajada_en: Anthropic grants researcher access to METR teams for independent evaluation of its models and safety practices, following the White House Accord. It also collaborates with SecureBio and Accenture on risk assessments.

title: The World Won't Wait: Evaluating and Teaching Agents Under a Live Clock
summary:
arXiv:2610.20665v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can solve complex interactive tasks, yet reasoning and tool calls take time. In continuously changing environments, an otherwise correct action may arrive too late. We introduce RealtimeBench, with 180 tasks across six game types, to evaluate agents while games continue running during inference. Paired evaluations show that GPT-6.1-sol outperforms the faster Jev when games are paused, but falls behind when they keep running. We propose Two-Timescale Offline Recursive Self-Improvement (TORSI): a slow teacher studies failures and tests corrections in paused games between attempts, then writes reusable instructions for a fast student. The student acts without teacher calls during gameplay, and validation scores determine which updates are adopted. Two rounds raise Jev's average test score from 13.51 to 24.19 on a 0--100 progress scale, improving all six game types. The instructions also improve average scores for three other models without retuning. These findings point toward real-time intelligence: enabling powerful LLM agents to remain effective in a continuously changing world by organizing deliberation, learning, and action across timescales.
title_es: RealtimeBench: evaluando agentes IA en tiempo real
bajada: Investigadores presentan RealtimeBench con 180 tareas para evaluar agentes IA en entornos dinámicos donde el tiempo es crítico. Proponen TORSI, una técnica de automejoría que permite a modelos rápidos aprender de modelos lentos pero precisos.
bajada_en: Researchers introduce RealtimeBench with 180 tasks to evaluate AI agents in dynamic environments where timing is critical. They propose TORSI, a self-improvement technique allowing faster models to learn from slower, accurate ones.

title: Evaluating Model Capabilities After Benchmark Saturation
summary:
arXiv:2610.20667v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Rapid advances in AI capabilities are causing benchmarks to saturate. Once several models approach perfect scores, a benchmark loses its power to differentiate between them, and with it its utility for informing AI safety cases and frontier policies. Yet benchmark items produce far more information than the scores we typically extract from them: a full transcript of how each model solved the task. We investigate whether these transcripts can be used to assess model capabilities even after benchmark scores have saturated. We simulate saturation retrospectively using historical benchmark and model releases, and test whether protocols that access only correctly solved transcripts from saturated benchmarks can predict capabilities measured on held-out, unsaturated items. We evaluate representative contemporary approaches for extracting information from model transcripts: pairwise judging, single-transcript absolute scoring, and predictions from deterministic transcript features or embeddings. We find that saturated transcripts retain capability information beyond benchmark accuracy. Amongst our evaluated protocols, pairwise judging performs best, reducing prediction error by 5.3 times compared to a baseline using only saturated benchmark scores. This capability-relevant information is distributed across transcript sections, but concentrated in specific channels of information such as reasoning and tool-calls. However, the predictive power of protocols does not always generalise across distribution shifts -- for example by underestimating the capabilities of the first reasoning models introduced in early 2025. Saturated benchmarks thus retain capability-predicting signal in their task transcripts, but extending the lifetime of existing benchmarks requires methods designed to extract these signals robustly.
title_es: Evaluando capacidades de IA después de saturación de benchmarks
bajada: Paper analiza cómo extraer información de utilidad de transcripts de modelos cuando los benchmarks tradicionales se saturan. Usando técnicas como pairwise judging, demuestra que hay señal de capacidad más allá de scores convencionales.
bajada_en: Paper analyzes how to extract useful information from model transcripts when traditional benchmarks saturate. Using techniques like pairwise judging, it shows capability signal exists beyond conventional scores.

title: [Research] 2,788 tokens/s on a single RTX 5090 with a diffusion LLM — Introducing ORL (fully open source) [R]

The GPU figures above are peak results on specific benchmarks, not averages across arbitrary prompts.We've open-sourced the models, training code, evaluation pipeline, and inference engine.What's the idea behind ORL?Unlike autoregressive LLMs, which generate one token at a time, diffusion LLMs can refine and finalize multiple tokens in parallel. But getting them to converge in fewer forward passes is challenging.Our approach has two key ingredients:1. On-policy residual learningInstead of predicting everything from scratch at each denoising step, the model carries forward its previous predictions as residual context and progressively refines them.The catch: these residuals are generated by the model itself, and their distribution changes during training. Training on stale, offline residuals creates a mismatch with inference.ORL addresses this by training directly on fresh trajectories generated by the current model, replaying the exact residual states encountered during inference.2. Learning to reduce uncertainty fasterSimply supervising the final output doesn't necessarily teach the model to converge faster.We introduceAdjacent Entropy Contraction, which encourages each denoising step to reduce uncertainty relative to the previous step. We also gate the loss to avoid unnecessarily p
title_es: ORL: 2,788 tokens/s en RTX 5090 con LLM de difusión
bajada: Nuevo método de investigación abierto (ORL) acelera modelos de lenguaje basados en difusión hasta 6.9x sin perder calidad. El resultado es significativo para developers que buscan inference rápido en hardware consumer.
